story.title: Nairobi Selected to Host 2029 World Athletics Championships
story.summary: Nairobi has been awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, marking the first time the event will be held in Africa. The Kenyan capital was chosen over competing bids from London, Munich, and Rome.

explore_lenses.label: Why did World Athletics choose Nairobi?
explore_lenses.title: A global-growth case backed by delivery plans
explore_lenses.summary: World Athletics said Nairobi prevailed on more than symbolism: it cited the bid's operational plan, government financial guarantees and potential to expand the sport's reach. The award also puts the next three editions in Asia, Africa and Europe.

claims.text: World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said the decision considered budgets, government financial guarantees, growth potential and analysis, alongside the historic significance of a first championships in Africa.
Coe's stated perspective was that Kenya's athletics culture and Nairobi's bid made this the appropriate moment to take the championships to Africa.
Munich was awarded the 2031 championships; London and Rome were unsuccessful for 2029, so the process allocated two future editions rather than simply selecting among cities for a single event.

explore_lenses.label: What must Nairobi deliver before 2029?
explore_lenses.title: Venue readiness and clean-sport scrutiny
explore_lenses.summary: Planning now shifts from the bid to delivering a September 2029 championship at Kasarani and maintaining confidence in Kenya's anti-doping system. The event will likely intensify attention on both issues.

claims.text: World Athletics says Nairobi 2029 is scheduled for September, following the Beijing 2027 championships; the governing body links this timing to making the championships the end-of-season global climax.
The Kasarani Stadium overhaul is a central readiness milestone because it is intended to precede both AFCON 2027 and the 2029 championships.

World Athletics said Kenya's government has committed $5 million annually to anti-doping, and a spokesperson argued that hosting could strengthen compliance by putting clean sport under greater scrutiny.
Forecast: scrutiny of Kenya's record of doping cases among elite runners is likely to grow as the country prepares to host, according to reporting by Sky News and Africanews.

story_report.summary: Nairobi will stage the 2029 World Athletics Championships, becoming the first African host of the event. The Kenyan capital was selected ahead of London, Munich and Rome, while Munich received the 2031 edition. World Athletics has scheduled the Nairobi championships for September, after Beijing hosts in 2027, positioning the event as the end-of-season global climax.

sections.heading: World Athletics selection rationale
sections.body: World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said the assessment included bid budgets, government financial guarantees, growth potential and analysis, as well as the significance of taking the championships to Africa for the first time. Coe said Kenya’s athletics culture and Nairobi’s bid made it the right moment for the continent to host. The governing body has not, however, published a detailed scoring breakdown or full comparison of the competing bids.

sections.heading: Nairobi readiness and doping scrutiny
sections.body: The overhaul of Kasarani Stadium is a central preparation milestone, with the work intended to be completed before both the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2029 championships. World Athletics said the Kenyan government has committed $5 million annually to anti-doping; a spokesperson said hosting could reinforce compliance by subjecting clean sport to greater scrutiny. Reporting by Sky News and Africanews indicates scrutiny of Kenya’s doping cases among elite runners is likely to intensify during the preparations.

related_stories.title: NATO Fighter Jets Intercept Drone Over Lithuania
related_stories.summary: NATO jets, specifically two Italian Eurofighter Typhoons, shot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace, believed to have entered from Belarus. The incident occurred between the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas, with no reported casualties or damage. While the drone's origin is suspected to be Belarus, the exact details remain unclear.
